- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp spike later, model underestimates breakout potential; adjust for lagged momentum.
- After a true price spike (e.g., >95), model often overcorrects or fails to peak early; reduce forecast peak height or add early plateau heuristic.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.20), model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer for downward correction or adjust mean reversion threshold.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day average by 2–5% in early cycles; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment for low-sentiment periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; add 1–2 day lagged mean reversion rule to forecast.
- Model underestimates true outcome when sentiment is positive but recent history is flat; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts.
